synopsis: DARPA announced RACER-SIM in January 2022 with Duality Robotics and Intel-Federal as its two prime contractors; its reported Phase 1 budget was approximately USD 6 million [f8419, f15831, f8420, f15832]. Duality, partnered with Neya Systems, was tasked with building an 80 km² virtual off-road environment measuring 20 km by 4 km on a digital-twin simulation platform [f8421, f15833]. Duality Falcon with the Neya autonomy stack is an explicitly supported RACER-Sim combination, although that compatibility claim is vendor-sourced [f8707]. RACER-Sim and NASA JPL provide independent evidence of Falcon's military off-road use, and JPL contracted the same platform for RACER Phase II in September 2024 [f8690, f8978, f15834]. This establishes military off-road relevance, but the corpus does not establish demonstrated construction or mining use for Falcon [f15889].
